science.title: Watching others pays off: Attentive macaques benefit from observing their group mates interacting
science.description: Monkeys constantly observe and evaluate their social environment. It stands to reason that the social and mental abilities required to do so were favored by evolution. After all, these abilities should influence how an animal interacts with its conspecifics and, as a result, what social position it can attain within the group's hierarchy. Researchers from the DPZ and the University of Göttingen have now investigated whether this widely held assumption is correct by studying 46 wild male Assamese macaques in Thailand. The paper is published in the journal Current Biology.

ai.title: Nvidia's investigation into CEO Huang's affair puts a spotlight on chip billionaire's personal life
ai.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is in the spotlight after revelations of an affair with a purported Chinese spy triggered a board investigation. Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 at a Denny's diner in San Jose, California. Born in Taiwan, he moved to the U.S. at age 9 and later studied electrical engineering at Oregon State University. He met his wife, Lori, there, and they both became chip designers in Silicon Valley. Known for his black leather jacket, Huang is seen as irreplaceable by tech analysts, who say Nvidia's success is heavily tied to him.
